newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end mixed in active trading.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end mixed in active trading.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended mixed in active trading on Thursday on improved sentiment, but profit-taking erased most of the morning's gains, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.256 points or 0.38 percent to 66.987 on volume of 19.8 million shares worth $9.1 million.
Shanghai's B share index rose after a securities official was quoted in the official media as saying he was confident of the development of the market.
"The news triggered active buying mainly from domestic investors, but overseas investors remained on the sidelines because most firms have yet to release their 1996 results," said one broker.

"Profit-taking emerged late in the session, wiping out most of the early rises," another broker said. "The index will consolidate around the current level unless some solid measures (to develop the market) are taken."
Textile maker Shanghai Haixin was the star on active buying, helped by expectations of an improvement in its 1996 results, rising $0.028, or 6.36 percent, to $0.468 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
Blue-chip Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor traded the most on profit-taking after continued rises over the past few days, falling $0.012, or 2.15 percent, to $0.546 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
Shanghai A shares reversed early gains on profit-taking, brokers said.
The index fell 6.799 points, or 0.63 percentm to 1,071.405 points on volume of 604.1 million shares worth 6.1 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index lost 10.387 points or 0.37 percent to 2,801.236 points.
United Hold was the biggest loser, falling 0.26 yuan, or 3.62 percent, to 6.92 yuan on volume of 844,276 million shares.
Shenzhen's A-share index ended up on investors' optimism over the market's medium-term outlook, but profit-taking pushed it off intraday highs, brokers said.
The A-share index firmed 2.17 points, or 0.58 percent, to close at 379.57 after hitting a high of 384.90 on heavy turnover of 9.67 billion yuan, up from 7.40 billion yuan on Wednesday.
The B-share index was unchanged at 151.74 points, with turnover falling slightly to HK$93 million from Wednesday's HK$97 million.

"Optimism over the market's medium-term outlook fuelled buying, given the stability of China's economic environment," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said. "But profit-taking emerged late in the session, pushing prices off intraday highs."
Brokers said they expected indices to rise next week after some corrections.
On the Shenzhen B-share market, property concern China Vanke Co was the top gainer, rising HK$0.24, or 3.97 percent, to HK$6.29 on volume of 321,600 shares.
Refrigerator manufacturer Hefei Meilin traded most on volume of 1.82 million shares, slipping HK$0.04 to HK$6.26 on profit-taking, brokers said.
Automobile components producer Weifu Fuel Injection, the biggest loser, slumped HK$0.09 to HK$4.81 with 177,200 shares changing hands.

On the A-share market, refrigerator producer Shaanxi Changling advanced 0.33 yuan to 7.27 yuan on the day's heaviest volume of 27.18 million shares worth 198 million yuan. Institutions bought the counter on anticipation of good 1996 results, brokers said.
